source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source C for crop/mung_bean in this knowledge base (Sources A-B were processed in Batch 42).
text: Bruchid/seed weevil (ខ្មៅត្រកួបផ្កា, printed as "Bruchid callosobruchus L.", family Bruchidae, order Coleoptera) females lay eggs on the pod surface; larvae bore into and feed inside pods or, after harvest, inside stored seed. The source states this pest can complete a generation in roughly 1 month and produce multiple generations within a year, making it a significant storage pest. Prevention and control listed together in the source: use timely, synchronized planting dates across a growing area; select disease/pest-free seed; follow recommended spacing and row layout; maintain field sanitation; scout fields regularly for pest and disease symptoms; and practice crop rotation. For chemical control, the source names Methyl-carbamate-group products such as Methyl phosphate (given as an example, likely referring to Dichlorvos) or a branded product "Atabron," noting that treatment is most effective when applied while the pest is still at the nymph stage, before it matures, since nymphs are easier to control. For long-term seed storage, the source separately recommends fumigation using Aluminium Sulphate at roughly 10 g per 70-100 kg of stored seed, sealed for roughly 80-88 hours in an airtight container.
caveat: "Methyl phosphate" is printed in the source in parentheses next to "Dichlorvos"-like phrasing; the exact active-ingredient identity intended is reported as printed rather than corrected, since "methyl phosphate" is not itself a standard insecticide active ingredient name.
